strings.mg.shunt.title: Shunting
strings.mg.shunt.subtitle: The shunter has a slip of paper, a whistle and no enthusiasm. Alexei has time.
strings.mg.shunt.instruction: Make up the evening train on track 1 as the slip says. Running in, the engine couples up everything standing there; where you uncouple, the wagons stay put.
strings.mg.shunt.waybill.title: Evening train · track 1
strings.mg.shunt.waybill.note: From the points to the buffer stop: plates, coal, tank. The covered wagon stays here.
strings.mg.shunt.status.home: The points are set for track {n}. The engine has {k} wagons on the hook.
strings.mg.shunt.status.in: Coupled up. The engine takes {m} of {k} wagons; the rest stay on track {n}.
strings.mg.shunt.fail.headshunt: Too long: the headshunt holds only the engine and two wagons.
strings.mg.shunt.fail.siding: Too full: track {n} holds only {cap} wagons.
strings.mg.shunt.fail.points_busy: The points are occupied. Pull out first.
strings.mg.shunt.solved: The evening train is made up. The shunter gives one short whistle – from him, that’s praise.
strings.mg.shunt.hint.1: Tip: Track 3 is empty. A wagon can wait there for a while.
strings.mg.shunt.hint.2: Tip: Start at the buffer stop. The tank wagon has to go onto track 1 first, on its own.
strings.mg.shunt.hint.next: Tip: Next, run onto track {n} and pull out again with {m} wagons.
strings.mg.shunt.hint.leave_first: Tip: Pull out again first, then think on.
strings.mg.chess.kicker: Karsk Railyard · under the signal-box stairs
strings.mg.chess.title: The chess game
strings.mg.chess.subtitle: Day shift against night shift, one move per shift, the pegboard set on a crate lid.
strings.mg.chess.instruction: The day shift (White) is to move and mates in two. The night shift answers on its own.
strings.mg.chess.sides: White: day shift. Black: night shift – queen, two rooks and checks of its own in reserve.
strings.mg.chess.note: “Night shift is better placed.” Below it, in another hand: “Wait and see.”
strings.mg.chess.status.second: Rxg8 – the night shift has no choice. Now the mate.
strings.mg.chess.fail.slow: Too slow: the night shift would have check at once, Qb1+, and the day shift nothing left.
strings.mg.chess.fail.check: Check – but the black king finds a way out.
strings.mg.chess.fail.nf7: Nf7+ Kg8 – and the king slips away via f8.
strings.mg.chess.fail.nomate: No mate. The night shift breathes on.
strings.mg.chess.fail.nxg8: Nxg8 only takes a rook. That’s no mate.
strings.mg.chess.solved: Mate. The night shift was better placed.
strings.mg.chess.hint.1: Tip: The night shift is threatening too. Only a move with check is fast enough.
strings.mg.chess.hint.2: Tip: The black king has no room to breathe. Whoever takes g8 from him wins.
strings.mg.chess.hint.3: Tip: The queen sacrifices herself on g8.
strings.mg.chess.hint.b1: Tip: A knight jumps over any wall.
strings.mg.chess.hint.b2: Tip: The knight from h6 to f7.
strings.mg.radio.title: The radio
strings.mg.radio.subtitle: Built in 1955, tuned to the Reichssender, as the house rules require. Beside the dial: a pencil dot.
strings.mg.radio.instruction: Turn the needle to the pencil dot and listen until the piece is over. When the porter’s newspaper drops, the needle must be back on the red line.
strings.mg.radio.status.reich: The Reichssender: light music, very orderly.
strings.mg.radio.status.foreign: Piano, double bass, brushes on a drum.
strings.mg.radio.fail.caught: The porter looks up. Konrad presses the Reichssender button, very calmly.
strings.mg.radio.solved: The piece is over. Konrad turns back, exactly onto the line.
strings.mg.radio.hint.1: Tip: When the paper drops, press the Reichssender button (R). The needle jumps straight back.
strings.mg.radio.hint.2: Tip: The magic eye closes when the station is tuned exactly. At the end, just nudge it.
